name: Deltoid / shoulder implants
lead: Deltoid or shoulder implants, in the context of looksmaxxing, refers to the idea of surgically placing a solid implant over or within the shoulder region to increase the apparent width or roundness of the shoulders. The deltoid is the muscle that forms the rounded contour of the shoulder and is the prime mover of arm abduction [1]. Broad shoulders are among the proportions discussed in appearance communities as part of a V-shaped upper body.

Published research located for this entry does not describe cosmetic deltoid implants. The surgical literature on shoulder implants concerns joint replacement (arthroplasty) for arthritis, fractures and rotator cuff disease, which is a different purpose and procedure [2][3]. No clinical study of implants placed solely to enlarge the shoulder contour was found, so this article is deliberately short.

paras: The deltoid has anterior, intermediate and posterior parts, originating on the clavicle, acromion and scapular spine and inserting on the humerus; together these fibers give the shoulder its rounded outline [1]. Visible shoulder width in a person is also influenced by the skeleton, notably the clavicles, which is why appearance discussions often separate bone width from muscle and soft-tissue volume.

Most published work on shoulder implants concerns prostheses that replace the glenohumeral joint. Examples include a laboratory study of how reverse shoulder implant design affects abduction range of motion [2], a Norwegian register study of revision risk after shoulder arthroplasty [3], and overviews of periprosthetic infection [4]. These studies address function, longevity and complications of joint prostheses and do not evaluate changes to outward shoulder appearance.
No studies found. Studies of shoulder arthroplasty exist [2][3][4], but they concern joint replacement for medical indications, not cosmetic enlargement of the deltoid or shoulder contour.

card.summary: Surgical shoulder-contour implants are talked about for width, but no cosmetic studies exist; the research is all joint replacement.
card.note: Surgical procedure; published implant research concerns joint replacement, not appearance.

quick.overview:
The idea is to place an implant to make the shoulders look broader or rounder. It is discussed as a surgical route to the wide-shoulder look.

No published study of implants used purely for shoulder appearance was found. Shoulder implant research covers joint replacement for medical conditions.
quick.mechanism: An implant would add volume over the deltoid or shoulder region, changing the outline. The deltoid itself is the muscle that rounds the shoulder contour.
quick.risks: As with any surgical implant, complications such as infection are documented in the joint-replacement literature, but the risks of a cosmetic shoulder implant have not been studied in the sources reviewed.
